final_candidates.decision_summary: V38D has the lowest fixed-backbone structural compatibility in the candidate pool and is absent from homologous sequences and strongly disfavored by the sequence model. Replacing buried/packing-compatible valine with aspartate is predicted to strongly disrupt PsaE folding.

V36D is strongly incompatible with the experimental PsaE backbone and receives near-minimal evolutionary and sequence plausibility. The hydrophobic-to-acidic substitution is a high-confidence folding-disruption design.

F40D is strongly structurally disfavored and replaces an aromatic hydrophobic residue with a charged acidic residue. It is also rare or absent among homologs and highly implausible to the sequence model.

stop_reason.detail: Three orthogonal evidence dimensions consistently prioritize V38D, V36D, and F40D, while the remaining tools do not directly assess PsaE folding disruption.

history.rationale: W17 is a bulky hydrophobic aromatic residue in the conserved N-terminal structured region; replacing it with an acidic residue should strongly disrupt local packing.
W17D is absent from homologs and implausible by the sequence model, although the fixed-backbone score suggests less direct structural disruption than the leading candidates.
W17D remains potentially disruptive because it removes a bulky aromatic residue, but its structural score indicates greater accommodation than top candidates.
Y18 directly follows W17 in a hydrophobic/aromatic segment. An acidic substitution is expected to be poorly accommodated in a folded hydrophobic environment.
Y18D imposes a large aromatic-to-acidic change with substantial structural incompatibility and no observed Asp among aligned homologs.
Y18D is structurally strongly disfavored and replaces an aromatic residue with an acidic residue, plausibly impairing the folded state.
I32 is within the central hydrophobic portion of the sequence. Introducing aspartate should destabilize packing without truncating the protein.
I32D is highly compatible with the fixed backbone despite being absent as Asp in the MSA, making folding disruption less likely than for the other core hydrophobic substitutions.
I32D is least favored because the structural model finds the mutant residue highly compatible with the experimental backbone.
Y34 is a bulky aromatic residue in the central structured region. Y-to-D removes hydrophobic packing and introduces an unfavorable charged side chain.
Despite evolutionary and sequence-model rejection of Asp, Y34D is compatible with the fixed experimental backbone and is therefore less compelling for folding disruption.
Y34D is retained as a fallback but has high structural compatibility, weakening the prediction of substantial folding disruption.
V36 lies in a dense I/V-rich stretch likely contributing to the folded core. Aspartate substitution is strongly nonconservative and likely destabilizing.
V36D is strongly disfavored by both backbone-conditioned and sequence-model evidence, while the site is evolutionarily constrained against Asp.
V36D is strongly disfavored by the fixed-backbone structural model and is therefore a leading folding-disruption candidate.
I37 is centrally located in a hydrophobic segment and is a strong candidate for core-packing disruption by an acidic substitution.
I37D is evolutionarily and sequence-model disfavored, but its backbone compatibility penalty is weaker than for V36D and V38D.
I37D shows moderate structural incompatibility and remains a credible disruptive substitution, but is weaker than neighboring V36D and V38D.
V38 precedes R39 and F40 in the central region. Replacing valine with aspartate should perturb local hydrophobic packing.
V38D has the most unfavorable fixed-backbone compatibility delta and is absent from the homolog MSA as Asp, consistent with a strongly disruptive hydrophobic-to-charged substitution.
V38D has the lowest structure-compatibility score among the pool, consistent with severe incompatibility on the experimentally resolved PsaE backbone.
F40 is a bulky hydrophobic aromatic residue likely important for structural packing. F-to-D is expected to be markedly folding-disruptive.
F40D is structurally and sequence-model disfavored, but naturally occurring Asp at this position reduces confidence that it will reliably abolish folding.
F40D has very low structural compatibility, supporting disruption from replacement of a hydrophobic aromatic residue with charged aspartate.
V43 is another hydrophobic residue in the central-to-C-terminal portion of PsaE. A charged replacement may reduce fold stability.
V43D is not tolerated by the MSA or sequence model, but its moderate backbone penalty makes it a lower-priority destabilization candidate.
V43D is structurally disfavored, although its incompatibility is less pronounced than the top hydrophobic-to-aspartate substitutions.
F48 occurs near the beginning of a glycine/serine-rich C-terminal segment and may anchor this region against the core. Replacing it with aspartate is a strongly disruptive change.
F48D has only a small backbone penalty and relatively higher sequence plausibility, while limited MSA coverage weakens the evolutionary inference.
F48D is only modestly prioritized because the backbone model indicates relatively high compatibility compared with leading candidates.
